title: Prefix fingerprinting, eviction signal correlation & long-context handoff - deep dive - PolarWave
summary: Deep technical troubleshooting session focused on odd eviction patterns correlated with prefix re-use and long conversational contexts. Discussed fingerprinting heuristics, spillback telemetry, VPC network jitter effects, and an experiment plan for localized KV retention tuning + synthetic benchmark reruns.

Schedule follow-up: 1 week after traces available (30m)
SE to provide tentative config patch for KV residency thermostat

Evan Chu - run synthetic workload and upload traces to shared S3 (due: 2027-03-08)

transcript:
Meeting header: 2027-03-02 10:10am PT, duration 1:02, recording enabled. Attendees listed.

[00:00:00] Sofia Ramos: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. We're going to dig into the eviction signals and this weird prefix reuse correlation you surfaced. Dev is on for the runtime side.
[00:00:12] Evan Chu: Thanks, Sofia. Quick context — we've been seeing periodic tail-latency spikes and a simultaneous uptick in eviction counts for certain prefix hashes. Pattern shows during long multi-turn sessions (2k+ tokens) but not consistent per user.
[00:00:28] Dev Patel: Got it, thanks. Before we jump in, can you confirm the deployment mode? Hosted or dedicated? Any VPC/private network in front?
[00:00:36] Riley Park: We're on Redwood Dedicated in our VPC peering setup. GPUs are p3-8 equivalent in a dedicated pool. We do have a NAT gateway and occasional network jitter from our cloud provider.
[00:00:48] Marta Klein: Also to add — we pin model version v2.3-quantized and we do a small amount of batching at the gateway (max batch 8, target latency 120ms).
[00:00:57] Dev Patel: Ok that helps. Two likely axes: KV residency + fingerprint collisions (prefix fingerprinting) and network-induced thundering during prefetch/handoff. We'll walk logs and outline experiments.
[00:01:12] Nina Ortega: Quick question: when you say fingerprint collisions, are you referring to the LRU keys or some prefix hash aliasing? We use conversation IDs + prefix window as keys.
[00:01:22] Dev Patel: Right, so Redwood's KV uses a 64-bit fingerprint of the prefix window. In rare high-cardinality workloads, different prefixes can map to same fingerprint (not common but possible). If fingerprints collide, eviction heuristics can evict incorrectly under pressure.
[00:01:38] Jordan Li: We've seen a few collision events flagged in telemetry but they seemed low frequency. The problematic periods show many evictions but users report context loss mid-conversation.
[00:01:48] Dev Patel: That suggests either collisions or spillback due to paged KV because the working set exceeded in-memory slab. When the slab spills to NVMe or remote store we do async prefetch which can increase tail latency and sometimes trigger eviction thrash.
[00:02:03] Evan Chu: We thought it was NVMe spill, but our disk ops look fine. During the spike we actually saw a network re-route and some small packet loss windows. Could packet loss cause eviction thrash?
[00:02:15] Dev Patel: Indirectly, yes. If prefetch RPCs to the backing store time out and the runtime believes the prefix isn't warm, it may evict entries to free slots for new incoming prefixes. Also, long-context requests keep KV open for longer which increases residency pressure.
[00:02:32] Sofia Ramos: Let's walk through the telemetry Dev wants to see. Dev?
[00:02:36] Dev Patel: I want span-level traces for: KV hit/miss per prefix fingerprint, eviction decision rationale (LRU vs GC vs forced), prefetch latency distribution, paged IO latencies, and kernel-level batch flush events. A small sample of affected conversation IDs is ideal.
[00:02:51] Nina Ortega: We can get conversation IDs. One oddity — prefixes with high semantic overlap (lots of repeated system prompts) appear to reuse the same token sequences but different user state, maybe that increases fingerprint reuse.
[00:03:04] Marta Klein: That's fingerprint reuse, not collision. Reuse is expected but it should be safe. The problem is when reuse leads to hot-prefix thrashing across shards.
[00:03:13] Dev Patel: Exactly. Fingerprint reuse -> hot prefix hotspotting -> eviction/stealing from other prefixes when slab pressure high. The runtime has a thermostat that aims to keep residency per slab under thresholds; if jitter or sudden bursts arrive it forces aggressive evictions.
[00:03:28] Riley Park: Is there a knob to increase per-prefix residency or reduce the thermostat aggressiveness? We've tried increasing slab size but that has cost impacts.
[00:03:36] Dev Patel: Yes, there's a residency thermostat parameter and a per-prefix priority hint you can set via the SDK. We can instrument a patch to give long-lived conversation prefixes a higher priority to avoid premature eviction.
[00:03:49] Jordan Li: What about fingerprint size? Can we move to 128-bit to reduce collision probability?
[00:03:54] Dev Patel: In theory yes, but that increases memory for the index and affects lookup performance; it's a tradeoff. First step is to confirm collisions versus reuse. We can also fingerprint with a salted hash per shard to reduce cross-tenant collisions.
[00:04:08] Eva(n) Chu: (laughs) yes, we are multi-tenant-ish in our pool and we saw collisions across different customers during a shared test. Could per-tenant salts be a mitigator?
[00:04:18] Dev Patel: Per-tenant salt is a low-cost mitigator for collisions. Also worth looking at our telemetry flags — we mark suspected collision events when two different prefixes map to same fingerprint and we see divergent token streams.
[00:04:31] Sofia Ramos: Security note — if you share conversation IDs with us, redact PII or send them in the secure S3 link we agreed in the NDA.
[00:04:39] Riley Park: Noted. We'll scrub identifiers.
[00:04:42] Nina Ortega: Back to the handoff — you mentioned async prefetch. Can that block generation threads? We have people seeing 200-500ms spikes mid-generation.
[00:04:51] Dev Patel: Prefetch is async but if prefetch misses and the runtime stalls waiting for certain KV entries to be available for the next batch, you can see tail effects. Also batching interacts: bigger batches amortize kernel work but increase exposure to a single slow prefetch. So your gateway batching of max 8 might increase tail when prefetch variance high.
[00:05:08] Jordan Li: Our batch size arrived from cost constraints. We can try reducing to 4 for certain routes if that helps.
[00:05:14] Marta Klein: Another lever is prefix sharding; we can tune prefix-to-shard mapping to reduce hot-prefix concentration. Use a dynamic sharding policy so hot prefixes spread across multiple slabs.
[00:05:25] Evan Chu: That's involved. We prefer config changes first.
[00:05:28] Dev Patel: Agreed. Let's define an experiment: 1) enable per-conversation priority hints for a small cohort, 2) temporarily reduce gateway batch size for that cohort, 3) enable per-tenant salt on fingerprinting in a canary pool, 4) collect span logs and kernel events.
[00:05:44] Nina Ortega: Sounds good. How long to see results?
[00:05:46] Dev Patel: Synthetic bench runs can show differences in a few hours. Production signals take 24-72 hours to stabilize. We'll want 72h windows ideally.
[00:05:55] Sofia Ramos: Marta, can you outline the config steps so PolarWave can apply them?
[00:05:59] Marta Klein: Sure. I'll send a one-page checklist: thermostat knobs (residency_threshold_ms, eviction_aggression), SDK hint pattern examples, salt toggle flag, and recommended batch size changes.
[00:06:11] Riley Park: About VPC jitter — we see occasional 50-200ms network spikes. Would increasing retry/backoff for prefetch help?
[00:06:18] Dev Patel: Increasing timeouts on prefetch RPCs has diminishing returns; better approach is to mark prefetch as best-effort and fall back to a lightweight local stub that returns partial context, while triggering async rehydrate. We can enable a degraded fallback policy to avoid blocking generation.
[00:06:32] Evan Chu: That might be acceptable. What's the cost to output quality?
[00:06:35] Dev Patel: Usually minor for short windows; the model will be missing some KV but you can use the longer context or repetition to recover. We'll include quality metrics in the experiment (perplexity, hallucination rate on a small eval set).
[00:06:45] Sofia Ramos: Good. Any security/compliance concerns with changing fingerprint salts?
[00:06:49] Marta Klein: No, salt is internal and doesn't change data residency. We should document it in the change log.
[00:06:55] Nina Ortega: One more weird artifact: we saw increased CPU interrupts aligning with eviction bursts. Could eviction GC be causing kernel-level stalls?
[00:07:02] Dev Patel: Eviction work is amortized, but when many entries get mass-evicted we trigger compaction and slab rebalancing which can spike CPU. We'll check kernel event timestamps against eviction peaks.
[00:07:14] Jordan Li: Ok. For the experiment, can Redwood provide a small patch to enable priority hints and salt toggle?
[00:07:19] Dev Patel: Yes — Dev and Marta will prepare a patch and a telemetry checklist. We'll also include a sample synthetic workload script for you to run that recreates high prefix reuse and long-context sessions.
[00:07:29] Evan Chu: Do you have a benchmark to simulate prefix reuse hotspots?
[00:07:32] Marta Klein: Yes, we have a synthetic harness that sends variable-length conversations with controlled prefix overlap and adjustable interarrival jitter. We'll share that.
[00:07:41] Sofia Ramos: Great. Let's confirm next steps and owners. Dev?
[00:07:44] Dev Patel: I'll send the telemetry checklist and sample span logs (owner). Marta will prepare patch and example config with thermostat deltas. Sofia will set up follow-up meeting.
[00:07:54] Evan Chu: We'll run the synthetic harness and upload traces to the secure S3 link.
[00:07:58] Riley Park: We'll also test reduced batch sizes on the gateway for a small cohort.
[00:08:02] Nina Ortega: We'll include a small red-team for quality checks.
[00:08:06] Sofia Ramos: Awesome. Anything else?
[00:08:09] Jordan Li: Just one last ask — can Redwood share any known past incidents docs about fingerprint collisions or thermostat misconfigurations?
[00:08:15] Marta Klein: We have a short incident playbook and a few internal retros. I'll redact and share the relevant bits.
[00:08:21] Sofia Ramos: Perfect. We'll follow up via email with the checklist and meeting notes. Thanks everyone.

[00:08:30] -- End of transcript --

Notes: Transcript includes pauses, slight overlaps, and occasional mis-hearings (e.g., "Readwood" for "Redwood"). Some timestamps approximate.
